attacks.claim: Auto-loading any package in node_modules with the `tasq-plugin` keyword (including nested/transitive deps) executes arbitrary code on every invocation, including in git pre-commit hooks and CI. Any transitive dependency or typosquat declaring the keyword gets code execution with no opt-in or allowlist, a major supply-chain escalation for a 180k/week tool.
attacks.evidence: Any installed package with the `tasq-plugin` keyword is picked up automatically. No more `plugins: [...]` array

attacks.claim: Discovery globs all of node_modules (`**/node_modules/**/package.json`) and parses every package.json on every invocation, before argument parsing. The benchmark shows regressions of ~17x for --version, ~6x for lint-staged, ~10x for cache-hit builds. This hits the pre-commit and editor hot paths and scales with install size. The artifact's claim that it is negligible is contradicted by its own table.
attacks.evidence: `tasq --version` | 0.11 s | 1.94 s ... `tasq run build` (cache hit) | 0.21 s | 2.02 s

attacks.claim: Claims are contradicted by or unsupported by the data. 'Cache hit under 50 ms of task time' conflicts with a 2.02 s wall time. 'Overall build time improves' rests on a 2.6 s cold delta that is within noise, and no cache-hit comparison shows improvement. Benchmarks use a single machine and a single repo.
attacks.evidence: Discovery is a fixed per-invocation cost and becomes negligible relative to real build work, so overall build time improves thanks to the new graph cache.

attacks.claim: Migration drops the `plugins` array and installs nothing, so existing users whose plugins are not keyword-tagged, or are not installed as discoverable packages, silently lose them. Local or path plugins and Yarn PnP projects (no node_modules) will have no discovery at all. The behavior is silent, with no warning. The glob may also follow symlinks in pnpm/workspaces and double-visit.
attacks.evidence: `tasq-migrate` removes the array and installs nothing new

attacks.claim: Discovery runs before argument parsing and reads all package.json with an unguarded JSON.parse. One malformed or unreadable package.json in node_modules crashes every command, including --version, and breaks commits/CI. No failure isolation or timeout is described.

The rollback plan only covers the `latest` tag. The `next`-first plan is good, but the blog and announcement go live at publish, before the 7-day soak, while promotion is later. The rollback of repointing `latest` to 2.9.4 doesn't undo the config migration (arrays removed by tasq-migrate, ESM rewrites) for users who already migrated, and a malicious-plugin incident cannot be undone by retagging.
attacks.evidence: Blog post and changelog go live at publish; ... re-point `latest` to `2.9.4`

attacks.claim: QA sample is small. Only 40 repos for migration, and the 15 smoke-tested plugins only show that they load. No test covers a hostile or malformed plugin, or the performance in large installs.
attacks.evidence: tested on 40 public repos, 38 fully automatic
